---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 5.1: estimates of the Bayesian models (pathologists)"
---

Step 5.1 of the paper simulation (pathologist design): point estimates (median) and 95 % quantile
intervals (QI) of recall, precision and F1 from every fit of the binomial + Poisson model of step 4.1.
The comparison with the truths of step 2.1 follows in the evaluation (step 7 and
`S3_Code_Simulation_Coverage.Rmd`).

The combined estimates are included in `simulation/estimates_pathologists/`; fits whose estimates
exist are skipped (see Run).

**Estimands** (marginal: over the slides and over the rater population)

| estimand | New pathologists per draw | averaging | Truth (step 2.1) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `average_pathologist` | K = 200 | pooled, grouped | `02_1_truth_average_pathologist.csv` |
| `single_pathologist` | the first of the K (a new random pathologist in every draw) | pooled, grouped | `02_1_truth_new_pathologists.csv.xz` (share of the per-rater truths inside the interval) |
| `observed_pathologists` | none: the observed pathologists with their estimated rater effects (as in Example 1) | pooled, grouped | `02_1_truth_average_pathologist.csv` (compared with the population of pathologists) |

- New pathologists: `posterior_epred()` with `allow_new_levels = TRUE, sample_new_levels =
  "gaussian"` on the observed slides (with their estimated slide effects) × K new raters. brms draws
  the rater effects of both parts jointly, with the rater SDs and the rater correlation of the draw,
  and uses the same effect on all slides of a new rater (checked on one fit per model).
- Recall and precision per cell as in `epred_recall_precision()` of step 5 (trials = 1), the expected
  counts per cell E[TP] = P · recall, E[FP] = E[TP] · (1 − precision) / precision.
- Bayesian bootstrap: Dirichlet(1, …, 1) weights over the slides, new for every draw, shared by all
  pathologists of a slide (no weights over the pathologists: the new pathologists already are a
  sample of the rater population).
  - pooled: weighted sums of the expected counts over slides and pathologists;
  - grouped: weighted mean of the per-cell metrics (cell = slide × pathologist).
- K = 200 (test on one fit per model): the noise of the K random pathologists widens the intervals
  of the average pathologist by about 2.5 % compared with K → ∞ (K = 50: about 8 %).
- Draws: all 4000 saved draws.

**Seed** (offset from `01_seed_offsets.csv`)

- `seed + 3000000` per fit: new pathologists and Dirichlet weights.
- The mirai daemons use the L'Ecuyer-CMRG random number generator (not R's default
  Mersenne-Twister); in a normal R session, set `RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")` first.

**Run**

- Parallel with `purrr::map()` and `in_parallel()` on mirai daemons (7 workers: one row per draw and
  cell, 4000 × 8000 rows, needs about 6–8 GB per worker).
- One file per fit. Fits whose estimates file exists are skipped, so the step can be restarted.

**Output** (`simulation/estimates_pathologists/`)

- `<model_id>/<scenario>_<n_slide>_v<variant>_r<rep>.csv`: estimates of one fit (new pathologists).
- `<model_id>_observed/<scenario>_<n_slide>_v<variant>_r<rep>.csv`: estimates of one fit (observed
  pathologists).
- `05_1_bayes_estimates.csv.xz`: all estimates combined: `scenario`, `n_slide`, `rep`, `variant`,
  `model`, `model_id`, `estimand`, `averaging`, `name`, `interval`, `value`, `.lower`, `.upper`.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
```

# Functions
```{r}
# F1-score from the counts (paper eq. 3); defined if TP = 0 (paper "Case B": 0)
calc_F1_score <- function(TP, FP, P) {
  2 * TP / (P + TP + FP)
}

# Median and 95% quantile interval (QI) of grouped draws (column value), one row per group
median_interval <- function(df) {
  median_qi(df, value) |>
    mutate(interval = "qi") |>
    select(-.width, -.point, -.interval)
}

# Columns for the binomial + Poisson model (as in step 3.1)
prepare_brms_data <- function(df_sim) {
  df_sim |>
    mutate(GroundTruth = TP + FN)    # Sensitivity/recall trials: all true objects (P)
}

# Pathologist estimates: per posterior draw K new pathologists on the observed slides
# (with their estimated slide effects), Bayesian bootstrap weights over the slides.
#   average_pathologist: all K new pathologists
#   single_pathologist:  the first new pathologist only (a new random pathologist in every draw)
# observed = TRUE: the observed pathologists with their estimated rater effects instead of new
# pathologists (average of the observed pathologists, as in Example 1)
#   observed_pathologists: all observed pathologists
# Recall and expected FP count per cell (trials = 1): precision = recall * P / (recall * P + FP)
bayes_pathologist_metrics <- function(fit, df_sim, K, observed = FALSE) {
  df_slides <- distinct(df_sim, slide, P)
  if (observed) {
    newdata <- distinct(df_sim, rater_ID, slide, P)
  } else {
    newdata <- crossing(rater_ID = paste0("new_", seq_len(K)), df_slides)
  }
  newdata <- newdata |>
    mutate(TP = 1, FN = 0, FP = 0) |>   # trials = 1: GroundTruth = 1
    prepare_brms_data()

  # Expectations per draw and cell (array draws x cells x part); every new pathologist gets
  # new rater effects in every draw
  e <- posterior_epred(fit, newdata = newdata, allow_new_levels = !observed,
                       sample_new_levels = "gaussian")
  n_draws <- dim(e)[1]

  # One row per draw and cell (as.vector() of the array: the draws vary fastest)
  df_draws <- tibble(
    .draw    = rep(seq_len(n_draws), nrow(newdata)),
    rater_ID = rep(newdata$rater_ID, each = n_draws),
    slide    = rep(newdata$slide, each = n_draws),
    P        = rep(newdata$P, each = n_draws)
  ) |>
    bind_cols(map(set_names(dimnames(e)[[3]]), \(part) as.vector(e[, , part])))
  rm(e)

  df_draws <- df_draws |>
    mutate(Recall = TP, Precision = TP * P / (TP * P + FP))

  # Bayesian bootstrap: Dirichlet(1, ..., 1) weights over the slides, new for every draw,
  # shared by all pathologists of a slide
  df_weights <- tibble(
    .draw  = rep(seq_len(n_draws), nrow(df_slides)),
    slide  = rep(df_slides$slide, each = n_draws),
    weight = rexp(n_draws * nrow(df_slides))
  )

  df_draws <- df_draws |>
    select(.draw, rater_ID, slide, P, Recall, Precision) |>
    mutate(TP = Recall * P, FP = TP * (1 - Precision) / Precision) |>
    left_join(df_weights, by = c(".draw", "slide"))

  if (observed) {
    df_estimands <- list(observed_pathologists = df_draws)
  } else {
    df_estimands <- list(average_pathologist = df_draws,
                         single_pathologist  = df_draws |> filter(rater_ID == "new_1"))
  }

  df_estimands |>
    imap(\(df, estimand) {
      df |>
        group_by(.draw) |>
        summarise(
          Recall_pooled     = sum(weight * TP) / sum(weight * P),
          Precision_pooled  = sum(weight * TP) / sum(weight * (TP + FP)),
          F1_pooled         = calc_F1_score(sum(weight * TP), sum(weight * FP), sum(weight * P)),
          Recall_grouped    = weighted.mean(Recall, weight),
          Precision_grouped = weighted.mean(Precision, weight),
          F1_grouped        = weighted.mean(calc_F1_score(TP, FP, P), weight)
        ) |>
        pivot_longer(matches("_(pooled|grouped)$"),
                     names_to = c("name", "averaging"), names_sep = "_") |>
        group_by(name, averaging) |>
        median_interval() |>
        mutate(estimand = estimand)
    }) |>
    bind_rows()
}
```

# Settings
```{r}
n_workers     <- 7
K             <- 200 # new pathologists per posterior draw
dir_fits      <- "simulation/fits_pathologists"
dir_estimates <- "simulation/estimates_pathologists"

# Short model ids for the file names (as in step 4.1)
df_models <- tribble(
  ~model,               ~model_id,
  "Binomial + Poisson", "binomial_poisson"
)
```

# Load data
```{r}
df_seed_offsets <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_seed_offsets.csv")
df_counts       <- read_csv("simulation/data/02_1_pathologist_observed_data.csv.xz")

offset_bayes <- df_seed_offsets |> filter(step == "bayes_postprocessing") |> pull(offset)
```

# Jobs
```{r}
df_jobs <- df_counts |>
  nest(data = c(slide, rater_ID, P, TP, FN, FP)) |>
  mutate(seed_bayes = seed + offset_bayes) |>
  cross_join(df_models) |>
  # new pathologists (average and single) and observed pathologists, own folders
  cross_join(tibble(observed = c(FALSE, TRUE))) |>
  mutate(
    file_name      = sprintf("%s_%d_v%d_r%03d", scenario, n_slide, variant, rep),
    file_fit       = file.path(dir_fits, model_id, paste0(file_name, ".rds")),
    dir_output     = if_else(observed, paste0(model_id, "_observed"), model_id),
    file_estimates = file.path(dir_estimates, dir_output, paste0(file_name, ".csv"))
  ) |>
  # only existing fits without estimates
  filter(file.exists(file_fit), !file.exists(file_estimates)) |>
  arrange(rep, scenario, n_slide, variant, model_id)

nrow(df_jobs)
```

# Estimates
```{r}
walk(file.path(dir_estimates, c(df_models$model_id, paste0(df_models$model_id, "_observed"))),
     \(dir) dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE))

mirai::daemons(n_workers)
invisible(mirai::everywhere(
  {
    setwd(dir_project)
    library(dplyr)
    library(tidyr)
    library(purrr)
    library(readr)
    library(brms)
    library(tidybayes)
  },
  dir_project = getwd(), K = K,
  calc_F1_score = calc_F1_score, median_interval = median_interval, prepare_brms_data = prepare_brms_data,
  bayes_pathologist_metrics = bayes_pathologist_metrics
))

t_start <- Sys.time()
df_errors <- df_jobs |>
  split(seq_len(nrow(df_jobs))) |>
  map(in_parallel(\(job) {
    tryCatch({
      fit <- readRDS(job$file_fit)

      set.seed(job$seed_bayes)
      bayes_pathologist_metrics(fit, job$data[[1]], K, observed = job$observed) |>
        mutate(scenario = job$scenario, n_slide = job$n_slide, rep = job$rep, variant = job$variant,
               model = job$model, model_id = job$model_id) |>
        select(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, model, model_id, estimand, averaging,
               name, interval, value, .lower, .upper) |>
        write_csv(job$file_estimates)
      NULL
    }, error = \(e) tibble(file_fit = job$file_fit, error = conditionMessage(e)))
  }), .progress = TRUE) |>
  bind_rows()
mirai::daemons(0)

difftime(Sys.time(), t_start, units = "hours")

# Failed fits (no estimates file, retried in the next run)
df_errors
```

# Combine
```{r}
# Only the per-fit files in the model folders (new and observed pathologists)
df_bayes_estimates <- list.files(file.path(dir_estimates, c(df_models$model_id,
                                                            paste0(df_models$model_id, "_observed"))),
                                 pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  read_csv()
write_csv(df_bayes_estimates, file.path(dir_estimates, "05_1_bayes_estimates.csv.xz"))

# Number of estimated fits per model, estimand and variant
df_bayes_estimates |>
  distinct(model, estimand, variant, scenario, n_slide, rep) |>
  count(model, estimand, variant, name = "fits")
```
